title: Checks for variable (and function) assignments that use the same names as builtins.
summary: Reusing a builtin name for the name of a variable increases the difficulty of reading and maintaining the code, and can cause non-obvious errors, as readers may mistake the variable for the builtin and vice versa. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-builtins and made it stable in v0.0.48.
message_templates: Variable `{}` is shadowing a Python builtin

title: Checks for function arguments that use the same names as builtins.
summary: Reusing a builtin name for the name of an argument increases the difficulty of reading and maintaining the code, and can cause non-obvious errors, as readers may mistake the argument for the builtin and vice versa. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-builtins and made it stable in v0.0.48.
message_templates: Function argument `{}` is shadowing a Python builtin

title: Checks for class attributes and methods that use the same names as Python builtins.
summary: Reusing a builtin name for the name of an attribute increases the difficulty of reading and maintaining the code, and can cause non-obvious errors, as readers may mistake the attribute for the builtin and vice versa. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-builtins and made it stable in v0.0.48.

title: Checks for imports that use the same names as builtins.
summary: Reusing a builtin for the name of an import increases the difficulty of reading and maintaining the code, and can cause non-obvious errors, as readers may mistake the variable for the builtin and vice versa. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-builtins and made it stable in 0.8.0.
message_templates: Import `{}` is shadowing a Python builtin

title: Checks for modules that use the same names as Python standard-library modules.
summary: Reusing a standard-library module name for the name of a module increases the difficulty of reading and maintaining the code, and can cause non-obvious errors. Readers may mistake the first-party module for the standard-library module and vice versa. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-builtins and made it stable in 0.9.0.
message_templates: Module `{}` shadows a Python standard-library module
